fix(style): keep the colour parser's reason in style parse errors (rich-diagnostics-un7.1) (#137)

Style.parse rewrapped every colour failure in a bare catch and threw the
original away, so `color(300)` reported only `Invalid style definition:
"color(300)"` while ColorSpec.parse on the same token knew the number was
out of range.

Both colour positions (foreground and `on` background) now go through one
helper that carries the colour error in the message and as `cause`:

  Invalid style definition "color(300)": ColorParseError: ColorSpec number
  300 is out of range (0-255)

StyleSyntaxError takes ErrorOptions so the cause can be chained. The
message prefix drops its colon (`Invalid style definition "x": reason`) so
the chain reads as one `what: why` sequence.
